text:
Avery: Thanks everyone — quick follow-up from today's all-hands. Dropping a leadership Q&A thread for anything we missed. I'll answer what I can and tag folks for specifics.

Priya: Quick one on messaging — how do we explain our mission to product teams that just want "model access"? They say: why not use the big cloud model APIs?

Avery: Short answer: we sell outcomes, not raw models. Focus on predictable latency/cost, rollout controls, and deployment parity (hosted/dedicated/private). One-liner suggestion: "Same API, predictable performance and cost at scale."

Marco: From infra — customers ask whether we compete with cloud infra or model providers. Which bits do we differentiate technically?

Avery: We sit between model vendors and infra. Differentiators: runtime optimizations (KV cache, continuous batching), smart routing + fallback policies, and deployment parity. We're the serving layer, not a model training shop.

Sam: Sales follow-up — for enterprise RFPs, lead with SLAs or cost comparisons? They always ask both.

Lina: Marketing request — can we get a one-pager for procurement: short bullets, clear asks?

Avery: RFP guidance: lead with SLA/availability and security (private options), then unit economics. I'll pair with @Lina and @Priya to draft it.

Tanya: A few customers asked if we'll open-source parts of the runtime or keep it proprietary as moat?

Marco: Plan is to open-source adapters and client libs, but keep the kernel/runtime IP internal. We'll publish a clear list of OSS components so customers know what's public.

Alex (ML): On models — will we publish recommended open models + quantization profiles per workload? Customers want a "reference stack."

Priya: Yes — we'll curate model+config bundles in the catalog (e.g., convo chat: model-X q4_0 + caching; embeddings: model-Y fp16). Make those first-class.

Avery: TL;DR on positioning vs competitors: we're the predictable-serving layer. Compete on operational guarantees and developer ergonomics, not on model R&D.

Sam: Sales objection: "Why not self-host?" Any concise rebuttals?

Avery: Self-hosting = higher ops cost and slower iteration. We offer reserved capacity and private deployments to hit security needs while reducing ops. Win themes: faster time-to-product and lower long-term TCO.

Lina: I'll draft the RFP one-pager plus a 2-slide positioning nugget for SDRs. @Avery — any must-have lines?

Avery: Include: "Unified runtime across hosted, dedicated, private" and "Cost controls: batching, caching, quantization recommendations." Also short customer quotes if available.

Tanya: Can we include a small performance SLO example for the one-pager? e.g., p95 < 150ms for small single-turn gen.

Marco: Here's a recommended SLO block:
```
SLO example:
- p50 < 80ms
- p95 < 150ms
- availability >= 99.9%
```

Avery: Awesome — thanks. Post additional follow-ups here and we'll fold them into the public summary doc. :sparkles:
